saints.name: St. David of Wales
saints.title: Bishop, Patron of Wales
saints.shortBlurb: The abbot-bishop of Menevia and patron of Wales, who taught his monks to be joyful and faithful in little things…
biography: David, in Welsh Dewi, was born about 500, the son of St. Non, and became a monk and famed teacher. He founded churches across Wales, chief among them his abbey at Mynyw, now St Davids, in Pembrokeshire, where his monks pulled the plough without oxen, lived on bread and water, and held nothing of their own.

At the Synod of Brefi about 550, tradition says, as he spoke against the Pelagian heresy the ground rose beneath him to form a hill and a white dove settled on his shoulder, and he was acclaimed primate of Wales.

He died on 1 March, in 589 or by another reckoning 601, his last words bidding his monks be joyful, keep the faith, and do the little things they had seen and heard in him; his cult was confirmed by Pope Callixtus II about 1120.

His shrine at St Davids drew pilgrims through the Middle Ages. As the chief teacher and father of the Welsh church he is venerated as the patron of Wales, his day on 1 March kept with the wearing of the leek.
saints.knownFor: Founding the monastery of Menevia and evangelizing Wales.

canonization.canonized: Canonized 1120 by Pope Callixtus II (per tradition)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 1 March
